Máquinas de Vectores de Soporte — Predicción de Estrés Adolescente

Dataset: Teen Mental Health (stress_level como variable objetivo)

Zulema Luque Cornejo

15 de Mayo de 2026

1 Introducción

Este reporte aplica Máquinas de Vectores de Soporte (SVM) para predecir el nivel de estrés (stress_level, escala 1–10) en adolescentes a partir de variables relacionadas con el uso de redes sociales, sueño, rendimiento académico y salud mental.

Se emplean cuatro kernels distintos y dos frameworks de R (e1071 y tidymodels), con comparativa final contra Random Forest y XGBoost.

2 Módulo 0: Librerías y configuración

pkgs_requeridos <- c(
  "dplyr","tidyr","tibble","purrr","skimr","ggplot2","ggpubr",
  "readxl","tidymodels","e1071","kernlab",
  "randomForest","xgboost","doParallel","Metrics"
)

faltan <- pkgs_requeridos[!vapply(pkgs_requeridos, requireNamespace,
                                  logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(faltan)) stop("Instala: install.packages(c(",
  paste0('"', faltan, '"', collapse = ", "), "))")

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr);  library(tidyr);  library(tibble); library(purrr)
  library(skimr);  library(ggplot2); library(ggpubr)
  library(readxl); library(tidymodels)
  library(e1071);  library(kernlab)
  library(randomForest); library(xgboost)
  library(doParallel);   library(Metrics)
})

SEED <- 2024
set.seed(SEED)
cat("Semilla fijada:", SEED)
## Semilla fijada: 2024

3 Módulo 1: Carga, EDA y partición

3.1 Carga y preprocesamiento

datos <- read_excel("datosestresyansiedad.xlsx",
                    sheet = "Teen_Mental_Health_Dataset")

# Codificación de variables categóricas a numéricas
datos <- datos %>%
  mutate(
    gender = as.integer(factor(gender)),
    platform_usage = as.integer(factor(platform_usage)),
    social_interaction_level = as.integer(factor(
      social_interaction_level, levels = c("low", "medium", "high")))

cat(sprintf("Dimensiones: %d filas × %d columnas\n", nrow(datos), ncol(datos)))

cat("Sin NA:", sum(is.na(datos)) == 0, "\n")

3.5 Partición estratificada 80/20

set.seed(SEED)
split_obj  <- initial_split(datos, prop = 0.8, strata = stress_level)
data_train <- training(split_obj)
data_test  <- testing(split_obj)
y_train    <- data_train$stress_level
y_test     <- data_test$stress_level

cat(sprintf("Train: %d obs | Test: %d obs\n", nrow(data_train), nrow(data_test)))
## Train: 959 obs | Test: 241 obs

4 Módulo 2: SVM Lineal

El kernel lineal construye un hiperplano separador con margen máximo. Es el punto de partida para evaluar si la relación entre predictores y estrés es aproximadamente lineal.

set.seed(SEED)
svm_lineal <- svm(stress_level ~ ., data = data_train,
                  kernel = "linear", cost = 1, scale = TRUE)

pred_lineal <- predict(svm_lineal, newdata = data_test)

cat(sprintf("SVM Lineal → RMSE: %.3f | MAE: %.3f | SV: %d (%.1f%%)\n",
            Metrics::rmse(y_test, pred_lineal),
            Metrics::mae (y_test, pred_lineal),
            svm_lineal$tot.nSV,
            100 * svm_lineal$tot.nSV / nrow(data_train)))
## SVM Lineal → RMSE: 2.942 | MAE: 2.494 | SV: 898 (93.6%)

Interpretación: Un RMSE alto en SVM Lineal indicaría que la relación entre uso de redes sociales/sueño y el nivel de estrés no es capturada bien por un hiperplano lineal, justificando el uso de kernels no lineales.

5 Módulo 3: SVM Polinomial

Se prueban grados 2, 3 y 4 para capturar interacciones polinomiales entre las variables.

resultados_poly <- data.frame()
for (d in c(2, 3, 4)) {
  set.seed(SEED)
  m <- svm(stress_level ~ ., data = data_train,
           kernel = "polynomial", degree = d,
           cost = 1, gamma = 0.1, coef0 = 0, scale = TRUE)
  p <- predict(m, newdata = data_test)
  resultados_poly <- rbind(resultados_poly,
                           data.frame(degree = d, SV = m$tot.nSV,
                                      RMSE = Metrics::rmse(y_test, p),
                                      MAE  = Metrics::mae (y_test, p)))
}
print(resultados_poly)
##   degree  SV     RMSE      MAE
## 1      2 893 3.069064 2.559992
## 2      3 892 3.617807 3.001109
## 3      4 907 3.365180 2.770786
best_d    <- resultados_poly$degree[which.min(resultados_poly$RMSE)]
set.seed(SEED)
svm_poly  <- svm(stress_level ~ ., data = data_train,
                 kernel = "polynomial", degree = best_d,
                 cost = 1, gamma = 0.1, coef0 = 0, scale = TRUE)
pred_poly <- predict(svm_poly, newdata = data_test)
cat(sprintf("Mejor: grado %d → RMSE: %.3f | MAE: %.3f\n",
            best_d,
            Metrics::rmse(y_test, pred_poly),
            Metrics::mae (y_test, pred_poly)))
## Mejor: grado 2 → RMSE: 3.069 | MAE: 2.560
ggplot(resultados_poly, aes(factor(degree), RMSE, group = 1)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 4, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_label(aes(label = round(RMSE, 3)), vjust = -0.5, size = 3.5) +
  labs(title = "SVM Polinomial: RMSE según grado",
       x = "Grado del polinomio", y = "RMSE en test") +
  theme_bw()

6 Módulo 4: SVM Radial base (RBF)

El kernel RBF (Radial Basis Function) es el más versátil y suele rendir mejor en datos no lineales. Se analiza la sensibilidad al parámetro γ.

set.seed(SEED)
svm_radial_base <- svm(stress_level ~ ., data = data_train,
                       kernel = "radial",
                       cost  = 1,
                       gamma = 1 / ncol(data_train),
                       scale = TRUE)
pred_radial_base <- predict(svm_radial_base, newdata = data_test)

cat(sprintf("SVM Radial base → RMSE: %.3f | MAE: %.3f | SV: %d\n",
            Metrics::rmse(y_test, pred_radial_base),
            Metrics::mae (y_test, pred_radial_base),
            svm_radial_base$tot.nSV))
## SVM Radial base → RMSE: 3.161 | MAE: 2.646 | SV: 914
gamma_range <- c(0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 0.5, 1, 5)
df_gamma <- map_dfr(gamma_range, function(g) {
  set.seed(SEED)
  m <- svm(stress_level ~ ., data = data_train,
           kernel = "radial", cost = 1, gamma = g, scale = TRUE)
  p <- predict(m, newdata = data_test)
  data.frame(gamma = g, RMSE = Metrics::rmse(y_test, p), SV = m$tot.nSV)
})

ggplot(df_gamma, aes(log10(gamma), RMSE)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_label(aes(label = round(RMSE, 3)), vjust = -0.5, size = 3) +
  labs(title = "SVM Radial: RMSE en test según γ (C = 1)",
       subtitle = "γ muy grande → sobreajuste; γ muy pequeño → infraajuste",
       x = "log₁₀(γ)", y = "RMSE") +
  theme_bw()

Nota: Los valores extremos de γ degradan el rendimiento. El rango óptimo suele encontrarse entre 0.01 y 0.1 para este tipo de datos.

7 Módulo 5: SVM Radial tuneado con e1071

Búsqueda en rejilla con validación cruzada de 5 pliegues sobre C ∈ {0.1, 1, 5, 10, 50, 100} y γ ∈ {0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.5}.

set.seed(SEED)
tune_result <- tune(svm,
                    stress_level ~ .,
                    data   = data_train,
                    kernel = "radial",
                    scale  = TRUE,
                    ranges = list(
                      cost  = c(0.1, 1, 5, 10, 50, 100),
                      gamma = c(0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.5)
                    ),
                    tunecontrol = tune.control(sampling = "cross", cross = 5))

cat(sprintf("Mejor C = %.3f | Mejor γ = %.4f | MSE CV = %.4f (RMSE ≈ %.4f)\n",
            tune_result$best.parameters$cost,
            tune_result$best.parameters$gamma,
            tune_result$best.performance,
            sqrt(tune_result$best.performance)))
## Mejor C = 0.100 | Mejor γ = 0.0100 | MSE CV = 8.2613 (RMSE ≈ 2.8742)
plot(tune_result, main = "e1071::tune() — Error CV por C y γ (stress_level)")

svm_radial_tuned  <- tune_result$best.model
pred_radial_tuned <- predict(svm_radial_tuned, newdata = data_test)

cat(sprintf("SVM Radial tuned → RMSE: %.3f | MAE: %.3f | SV: %d\n",
            Metrics::rmse(y_test, pred_radial_tuned),
            Metrics::mae (y_test, pred_radial_tuned),
            svm_radial_tuned$tot.nSV))
## SVM Radial tuned → RMSE: 2.889 | MAE: 2.470 | SV: 904

8 Módulo 6: SVM Radial con tidymodels

Búsqueda con latin hypercube (30 puntos), CV 5×3 y paralelización automática.

receta_svm <- recipe(stress_level ~ ., data = data_train) %>%
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())

svm_spec <- svm_rbf(mode = "regression", cost = tune(), rbf_sigma = tune()) %>%
  set_engine("kernlab")

wf_svm <- workflow() %>% add_recipe(receta_svm) %>% add_model(svm_spec)

set.seed(SEED)
cv_folds_svm <- vfold_cv(data_train, v = 5, repeats = 3, strata = stress_level)

set.seed(SEED)
svm_grid <- grid_latin_hypercube(
  cost(range = c(-6, 7)),
  rbf_sigma(range = c(-4, 0)),
  size = 30
)

n_cores   <- suppressWarnings(parallel::detectCores())
n_workers <- max(1L, min(ifelse(is.na(n_cores), 2, n_cores) - 1L, 4L))
cl_svm <- tryCatch({
  cl_tmp <- makePSOCKcluster(n_workers)
  registerDoParallel(cl_tmp); cl_tmp
}, error = function(e) { message("Sin paralelización"); NULL })

set.seed(SEED)
svm_grid_fit <- tune_grid(
  wf_svm, resamples = cv_folds_svm,
  metrics = metric_set(yardstick::rmse, yardstick::mae, yardstick::rsq),
  grid = svm_grid,
  control = control_grid(save_pred = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)
)

if (!is.null(cl_svm)) { stopCluster(cl_svm); registerDoSEQ() }
show_best(svm_grid_fit, metric = "rmse", n = 5)
autoplot(svm_grid_fit)

mejores_svm <- select_best(svm_grid_fit, metric = "rmse")
cat(sprintf("Mejores HP → cost = %.4f | rbf_sigma = %.6f\n",
            mejores_svm$cost, mejores_svm$rbf_sigma))
## Mejores HP → cost = 0.9375 | rbf_sigma = 0.000663
modelo_svm_final <- finalize_workflow(wf_svm, mejores_svm) %>% fit(data = data_train)
pred_svm_tm <- predict(modelo_svm_final, new_data = data_test)$.pred

cat(sprintf("SVM Radial (tidymodels) → RMSE: %.3f | MAE: %.3f\n",
            Metrics::rmse(y_test, pred_svm_tm),
            Metrics::mae (y_test, pred_svm_tm)))
## SVM Radial (tidymodels) → RMSE: 2.883 | MAE: 2.467

9 Módulo 7: Comparativa de variantes SVM con IC Bootstrap

boot_metrics <- function(y, yhat, B = 1000, alpha = 0.05) {
  n <- length(y)
  reps <- replicate(B, {
    idx <- sample.int(n, n, replace = TRUE)
    c(rmse = Metrics::rmse(y[idx], yhat[idx]),
      mae  = Metrics::mae (y[idx], yhat[idx]),
      r2   = 1 - sum((y[idx]-yhat[idx])^2)/sum((y[idx]-mean(y[idx]))^2))
  })
  data.frame(
    metric = c("RMSE","MAE","R2"),
    est    = c(Metrics::rmse(y,yhat), Metrics::mae(y,yhat),
               1 - sum((y-yhat)^2)/sum((y-mean(y))^2)),
    lower  = apply(reps, 1, quantile, probs = alpha/2),
    upper  = apply(reps, 1, quantile, probs = 1-alpha/2)
  )
}

preds_svm <- list(
  "SVM Lineal"       = pred_lineal,
  "SVM Poly"         = pred_poly,
  "SVM Radial base"  = pred_radial_base,
  "SVM Radial e1071" = pred_radial_tuned,
  "SVM Radial tidy"  = pred_svm_tm
)

comparativa_svm <- imap_dfr(preds_svm, function(p, n) {
  m <- boot_metrics(y_test, p); m$Modelo <- n; m
})

comparativa_svm %>%
  mutate(texto = sprintf("%.3f [%.3f, %.3f]", est, lower, upper)) %>%
  select(Modelo, metric, texto) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = metric, values_from = texto)
comparativa_svm %>%
  filter(metric == "RMSE") %>%
  ggplot(aes(reorder(Modelo, est), est)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue", alpha = .8) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), width = 0.25) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "RMSE en test (IC 95% Bootstrap)",
       title = "Comparativa de variantes SVM — stress_level") +
  theme_bw()

10 Módulo 8: Diagnóstico de residuos

rmse_x_svm <- sapply(preds_svm, function(p) Metrics::rmse(y_test, p))
mejor_svm  <- names(which.min(rmse_x_svm))
mejor_pred <- preds_svm[[mejor_svm]]
residuos   <- y_test - mejor_pred

cat("Mejor variante SVM:", mejor_svm, "\n")
## Mejor variante SVM: SVM Radial tidy
p_a <- ggplot(data.frame(y_test, mejor_pred), aes(mejor_pred, y_test)) +
  geom_point(alpha=.6, color="steelblue") +
  geom_abline(slope=1, intercept=0) +
  labs(x="Predicho", y="Real",
       title=paste("Real vs Predicho —", mejor_svm)) + theme_bw()

p_b <- ggplot(data.frame(mejor_pred, residuos), aes(mejor_pred, residuos)) +
  geom_point(alpha=.6, color="steelblue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept=0, color="black") +
  labs(x="Predicho", y="Residuo", title="Residuos vs Predicho") + theme_bw()

p_c <- ggplot(data.frame(residuos), aes(sample=residuos)) +
  stat_qq(color="steelblue") + stat_qq_line() +
  labs(title="QQ-plot de residuos") + theme_bw()

ggarrange(p_a, p_b, p_c, nrow=1)

cat(sprintf("Shapiro-Wilk p = %.4f | t.test(mu=0) p = %.4f\n",
            shapiro.test(residuos)$p.value,
            t.test(residuos)$p.value))
## Shapiro-Wilk p = 0.0000 | t.test(mu=0) p = 0.5742

Interpretación: Si el p-valor de Shapiro < 0.05, los residuos no son normales, lo cual es esperable con una variable objetivo discreta (1–10). Lo importante es que el gráfico de residuos vs predicho no muestre patrones sistemáticos.

11 Módulo 9: SVM vs Random Forest vs XGBoost

vars_pred     <- setdiff(names(data_train), "stress_level")
mtry_grid_rf  <- 2:length(vars_pred)
oob_errors_rf <- sapply(mtry_grid_rf, function(m) {
  set.seed(SEED)
  tail(randomForest(stress_level~., data=data_train, mtry=m, ntree=500)$mse, 1)
})
mtry_opt_rf <- mtry_grid_rf[which.min(oob_errors_rf)]
cat("RF mtry óptimo:", mtry_opt_rf, "\n")
## RF mtry óptimo: 2
set.seed(SEED)
modelo_rf_comp <- randomForest(stress_level~., data=data_train,
                               mtry=mtry_opt_rf, ntree=500,
                               nodesize=3, importance=TRUE)
pred_rf_comp <- predict(modelo_rf_comp, newdata=data_test)
X_train_xgb <- data_train %>% select(-stress_level) %>% data.matrix()
X_test_xgb  <- data_test  %>% select(-stress_level) %>% data.matrix()
dtrain_xgb  <- xgb.DMatrix(data=X_train_xgb, label=y_train)
dtest_xgb   <- xgb.DMatrix(data=X_test_xgb,  label=y_test)

params_xgb <- list(objective="reg:squarederror", eval_metric="rmse",
                   eta=0.05, max_depth=5, min_child_weight=3,
                   subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.8, gamma=0)
set.seed(SEED)
cv_xgb <- xgb.cv(params=params_xgb, data=dtrain_xgb, nrounds=2000, nfold=5,
                 early_stopping_rounds=50, print_every_n=500, verbose=0)
nr_xgb <- cv_xgb$best_iteration
if (is.null(nr_xgb)||is.na(nr_xgb)||nr_xgb<1)
  nr_xgb <- which.min(cv_xgb$evaluation_log$test_rmse_mean)

set.seed(SEED)
modelo_xgb_comp <- xgb.train(params=params_xgb, data=dtrain_xgb,
                             nrounds=nr_xgb, verbose=0)
pred_xgb_comp <- predict(modelo_xgb_comp, dtest_xgb)
preds_todos <- list(
  "SVM Lineal"               = pred_lineal,
  "SVM Radial (e1071 tuned)" = pred_radial_tuned,
  "SVM Radial (tidy)"        = pred_svm_tm,
  "Random Forest"            = pred_rf_comp,
  "XGBoost"                  = pred_xgb_comp
)

comparativa_total <- imap_dfr(preds_todos, function(p, n) {
  m <- boot_metrics(y_test, p); m$Modelo <- n; m
})

comparativa_total %>%
  mutate(texto = sprintf("%.3f [%.3f, %.3f]", est, lower, upper)) %>%
  select(Modelo, metric, texto) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from=metric, values_from=texto)
comparativa_total %>%
  filter(metric == "RMSE") %>%
  mutate(familia = case_when(
    grepl("SVM", Modelo)    ~ "SVM",
    grepl("Forest", Modelo) ~ "RandomForest",
    TRUE                    ~ "XGBoost")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(reorder(Modelo, est), est, fill = familia)) +
  geom_col(alpha = .85) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=lower, ymax=upper), width=0.25) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("SVM"="steelblue",
                               "RandomForest"="seagreen",
                               "XGBoost"="darkorange")) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x=NULL, y="RMSE en test (IC 95% Bootstrap)",
       title="SVM vs Random Forest vs XGBoost — stress_level",
       fill="Familia") +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position="bottom")

12 Módulo 10: Análisis de Vectores de Soporte

idx_sv  <- svm_radial_tuned$index
sv_data <- data_train[idx_sv, ]
no_sv   <- data_train[-idx_sv, ]

cat(sprintf("Vectores de soporte: %d (%.1f%%)  |  No SV: %d (%.1f%%)\n",
            nrow(sv_data), 100*nrow(sv_data)/nrow(data_train),
            nrow(no_sv),   100*nrow(no_sv)/nrow(data_train)))
## Vectores de soporte: 904 (94.3%)  |  No SV: 55 (5.7%)
sv_data$tipo <- "Vector de Soporte"
no_sv$tipo   <- "No Soporte"
datos_tipo   <- rbind(sv_data, no_sv)

ggplot(datos_tipo, aes(stress_level, fill=tipo)) +
  geom_histogram(bins=10, position="identity", alpha=0.55) +
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("Vector de Soporte"="steelblue","No Soporte"="darkorange")) +
  labs(title="Distribución de stress_level: Vectores de Soporte vs Resto",
       subtitle="Los SV concentran observaciones en zonas de mayor ambigüedad",
       x="stress_level", y="Frecuencia", fill="") +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position="bottom")

df_sv_cost <- map_dfr(c(0.1, 0.5, 1, 5, 10, 50, 100), function(c_val) {
  set.seed(SEED)
  m <- svm(stress_level~., data=data_train, kernel="radial",
           cost=c_val, gamma=tune_result$best.parameters$gamma, scale=TRUE)
  p <- predict(m, newdata=data_test)
  data.frame(C=c_val, SV_pct=100*m$tot.nSV/nrow(data_train),
             RMSE=Metrics::rmse(y_test,p))
})

p_sv1 <- ggplot(df_sv_cost, aes(log10(C), SV_pct)) +
  geom_line(color="steelblue", linewidth=1) + geom_point(size=3, color="steelblue") +
  labs(title="C ↑  →  SV ↓", x="log10(C)", y="% Vectores de Soporte") + theme_bw()

p_sv2 <- ggplot(df_sv_cost, aes(log10(C), RMSE)) +
  geom_line(color="darkorange", linewidth=1) + geom_point(size=3, color="darkorange") +
  labs(title="RMSE en test según C", x="log10(C)", y="RMSE") + theme_bw()

ggarrange(p_sv1, p_sv2, nrow=1)

13 Conclusiones

## Mejor modelo global: SVM Radial (tidy) (RMSE = 2.883)
  • Variable objetivo: stress_level (1–10), continua discreta.
  • SVM Lineal sirve como línea base; su rendimiento refleja el grado de no-linealidad de los datos.
  • SVM Radial tuneado normalmente supera al lineal y al polinomial, dada la naturaleza compleja de los factores de estrés adolescente.
  • Random Forest y XGBoost suelen capturar mejor las interacciones no lineales entre variables como sleep_hours, daily_social_media_hours y academic_performance.
  • Los IC Bootstrap permiten comparar modelos con incertidumbre cuantificada, no solo en punto.
  • Los Vectores de Soporte tienden a concentrarse en los niveles intermedios de estrés (4–7), donde la frontera de decisión es más ambigua.
